description.short_caption: Erythematous lesion with central necrosis on the lower extremity.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of the lower extremity, specifically the knee region. There is a well-demarcated erythematous lesion with a central area of necrosis or ulceration. Surrounding the lesion, the skin appears inflamed with some induration. The lesion suggests a possible infectious or inflammatory etiology.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing a large cell with intracellular organisms.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a large cell with a pink cytoplasm and multiple dark-staining intracellular organisms. The background consists of numerous smaller cells with dense nuclei, likely inflammatory cells. The staining technique highlights the contrast between the large cell and the surrounding tissue. The organisms appear clustered within the cytoplasm, suggesting an infectious process.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), shows granulomatous inflammation characterized by a dense collection of inflammatory cells, including epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells. A central area of necrosis is visible, suggesting caseating granulomas. The surrounding tissue shows lymphocytic infiltration. These findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, such as tuberculosis or fungal infection.
